The '''Association for Symbolic Logic''' ('''ASL''') is an [[international organization]] of specialists in [[mathematical logic]] and [[philosophical logic]]. The ASL was founded in 1936, and its first president was [[Curt John Ducasse]]. The current president of the ASL is [[Natasha Dobrinen]].<ref>{{cite journal|title=Association for Symbolic Logic|journal=The Bulletin of Symbolic Logic|volume=31|issue=1|date=March 2025|pages=188–193|jstor=27379752}}</ref>

== Publications ==

The ASL publishes [[book]]s and [[academic journal]]s. Its three official journals are:
* ''[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]]'' – publishes research in all areas of mathematical logic.  Founded in 1936, {{issn|0022-4812}}.
* ''Bulletin of Symbolic Logic'' – publishes primarily expository articles and reviews. Founded in 1995, ISSN 1079-8986. ([https://www.cambridge.org/core/journals/bulletin-of-symbolic-logic Cambridge Core])
* ''Review of Symbolic Logic'' – publishes research relating to logic, philosophy, science, and their interactions. Founded in 2008, {{issn|1755-0203}}.

In addition, the ASL has a sponsored journal:  
* ''Journal of Logic and Analysis''  publishes research on the interactions between mathematical logic and pure and applied analysis.  Founded in 2009 as an [[open-access journal|open-access]] successor to the Springer journal ''Logic and Analysis''. {{issn|1759-9008}}.

The organization played a part in publishing the collected writings of [[Kurt Gödel]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/godel-lecturers/ |title=Gödel Lecturers – Association for Symbolic Logic |access-date=21 February 2019 |archive-date=22 December 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191222154857/http://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/godel-lecturers/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

== Gödel Lecture Series ==
The [[Gödel Lecture]] Series is series of annual ASL lectures that trace back to 1990.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Gödel Lecturers – Association for Symbolic Logic |url=https://aslonline.org/prizes-and-awards/godel-lecturers/ |access-date=2024-02-29 |language=en-US |archive-date=12 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240212001921/https://aslonline.org/prizes-and-awards/godel-lecturers/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

'''The Thirty-Fifth Gödel Lecture 2024'''

[[T. M. Scanlon|Thomas Scanlon]], (Un)decidability in fields

'''The Thirty-Fourth Gödel Lecture 2023'''

[[Carl Jockusch]], From algorithms which succeed on a large set of inputs to the [[Turing degree|Turing degrees]] as a [[metric space]]

'''The Thirty-Third Gödel Lecture 2022'''

[[Patricia Blanchette]], Formalism in Logic

'''The Thirty-Second Gödel Lecture 2021'''

[[Matthew Foreman]], Gödel [[Diffeomorphism|Diffeomorphisms]]

[[Élisabeth Bouscaren|Elisabeth Bouscaren]], The ubiquity of configurations in [[Model theory|Model Theory]]

'''The Thirtieth Gödel Lecture 2019'''

'''The Twenty-Ninth Annual Gödel Lecture 2018'''

[[Rod Downey]], Algorithmic randomness

'''The Twenty-Seventh Annual Gödel Lecture 2016'''

'''The Twenty-Sixth Annual Gödel Lecture 2015'''

'''The Twenty-Fifth Annual Gödel Lecture 2014'''

'''The Twenty-Fourth Annual Gödel Lecture 2013'''

[[Kit Fine]], [[Truthmaker theory|Truthmaker]] semantics

'''The Twenty-Third Annual Gödel Lecture 2012'''

[[John R. Steel|John Steel]], The hereditarily ordinal definable sets in models of determinacy

'''The Twenty-Second Annual Gödel Lecture 2011'''

[[Anand Pillay]], [[First order theories]]

'''The Twenty-First Annual Gödel Lecture 2010'''

[[Alexander Razborov]], Complexity of propositional proofs

'''The Twentieth Annual Gödel Lecture 2009'''

[[Richard Shore]], Reverse Mathematics: the Playground of Logic

'''The Nineteenth Annual Gödel Lecture 2008'''

[[W. Hugh Woodin]], The Continuum Hypothesis, the [[Ω-conjecture|Ω Conjecture]], and the inner model problem of one [[supercompact cardinal]]

'''The Eighteenth Annual Gödel Lecture 2007'''

== Meetings ==

The ASL holds two main meetings every year, one in North America and one in Europe (the latter known as the ''Logic Colloquium''). In addition, the ASL regularly holds joint meetings with both the [[American Mathematical Society]] ("AMS") and the [[American Philosophical Association]] ("APA"), and sponsors meetings in many different countries every year.

==Awards==
The association periodically presents a number of prizes and awards.<ref>{{cite web|url = https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/|title = Prizes and Awards – Association for Symbolic Logic|publisher = Association of Symbolic Logic|access-date = 24 January 2019|archive-date = 24 January 2019|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20190124203319/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/|url-status = live}}</ref>

===Karp Prize===
The Karp Prize is awarded by the association every five years for an outstanding paper or book in the field of symbolic logic. It consists of a cash award and was established in 1973 in memory of Professor [[Carol Karp]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |title=Karp Prize Recipients – Association for Symbolic Logic |access-date=24 January 2019 |archive-date=22 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

===Sacks Prize===
The Sacks Prize is awarded for the most outstanding doctoral dissertation in mathematical logic. It consists of a cash award and was established in 1999 to honor Professor [[Gerald Sacks]] of MIT and Harvard.

===Shoenfield Prize===
Inaugurated in 2007, the Shoenfield Prize is awarded every three years in two categories, book and article, recognizing outstanding expository writing in the field of logic and honoring the name of [[Joseph R. Shoenfield]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/shoenfield-prize-recipients/ |title=Shoenfield Prize Recipients – Association for Symbolic Logic |access-date=21 February 2019 |archive-date=22 July 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/shoenfield-prize-recipients/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>
